## The Problem

As the UK transitions to clean energy, grid operators need to know **where** 
to prioritise asset upgrades and **which** power generators are best suited 
for conversion to renewable sources. Northern Power Grid needed data-driven 
answers to both questions.

This project was completed as part of the Data Study Group at 
**The Alan Turing Institute**.

## Approach

I analysed spatial and temporal patterns in power consumption and station 
capacity across the northern UK. To identify stations under the most strain, 
I applied **Extreme Value Theory** — a statistical technique for modelling 
the probability of rare but significant deviations from normal behaviour.

The outputs included visualisations of stations where asset upgrades are 
required and recommendations for which power generators should be prioritised 
for conversion to solar and wind.

## Tools & Techniques

- Extreme Value Theory
- Geospatial visualisation
- Time-series analysis
- Python
